# caption_verify

**In one sentence:** The Caption Verifier modal. For each image it renders a picture from that image's caption, so you can judge whether the text encoder really understands the words, and edit the caption if it does not.

## Why it exists
A caption only helps LoRA training if the base model's text encoder knows its terms. This screen lets you test that. You render from the caption, compare the result with the source photo, and mark the caption "renders correctly", "renders generic" or "renders wrong". It is the UI half of the caption-verifier pipeline step (`prepare_lora_kit/steps/caption_verifier/step.py`).

## What's inside
| File / folder | What it does |
|---|---|
| `caption_verify.js` | `showCaptionVerify(pending, { onSubmitted })` creates a `CaptionVerify` class. It handles selection, keyboard shortcuts, editing, verdicts, running renders, the elapsed-time counter, and submitting. |
| `caption_verify.css` | Styles for the workspace, editor, verdict buttons, compare pane, notices and filmstrip (`.caption-verify-*`). |
| `components/` | Modal frame, caption editor, preview pane and filmstrip tiles. |
| `utils/` | Caption store, preview store and the verdict list (no DOM code). |

## How it works
- The job controller opens this modal when Python posts a pending interaction of kind `caption_verify`. The payload holds `items` (path, name, caption, image URIs, `initial_verdict`) and `settings` (`model_id`).
- Moving through images never starts a render. Rendering is a GPU job, and the first one also loads the model (it can take minutes). It runs only on a click or on Ctrl+Enter, through `api().generate_caption_preview(jobId, path, caption, { reroll })`.
- Only one render runs at a time. Its result is stored under the image path it was started for.
- Live model-load status comes from the `plk:job-status` event. A local one-second timer updates the wait label.
- Keys: `1` / `2` / `3` set the verdict, the left and right arrows move between images. These keys are ignored while you are typing in the caption box.
- "Continue" sends `buildSubmitValue(...)` through `api().submit_interaction`. Cancel removes the listeners and closes the modal.

## Who uses it
- `static/job/controller.js`: calls `showCaptionVerify` for `pending.kind === "caption_verify"`.
- `static/styles.css`: `@import`s `caption_verify.css`.
- Python side: `prepare_lora_kit_ui/runner/caption_verify_interaction.py` (builds the payload) and `prepare_lora_kit_ui/bridge.py` (`generate_caption_preview`).
- Tests: `tests/ui/static/caption_verify.test.js`.

## Good to know
- Verdicts loaded from an earlier session (not `correct`) count as already reviewed, so their tiles show the remembered answer.
- A token count is shown only after a render for the exact text on screen. Editing the caption hides it again.
